svg.title: Record Access and Escalation Costs
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-record-access-cost-reference; chapter number: 3; title: Record Access and Escalation Costs; subtitle: Keep a record lookup, a preliminary title search, and a probate proceeding financially distinct.; caption: GenealogyMagazine quotes ordinary courthouse copies; Matt Hecker on Logan Fullmer quotes Smart Skip; Seth on REtipster quotes portfolio-result viewing; Jamel Gibbs quotes preliminary title searches; Al Nicoletti on Courtney Fricke quotes a single probate.; assumptions note: These GenealogyMagazine, Matt Hecker, Seth, Jamel Gibbs, and Al Nicoletti figures are independent US-dollar price references. Every bar is a standalone total, not a cumulative balance, deduction, or profit calculation. The title-search endpoints are alternatives within one quoted range.; note: GenealogyMagazine excludes vital records from its usual copy price and notes higher certification charges. Seth's surcharge applies upon viewing results. Nicoletti's approximately $4,000–$4,500 example is not a document-retrieval fee.; chart type: waterfall; bars: label: Smart Skip search; value: 0.15; display: $0.15 per skip trace; kind: total; label: Portfolio-result viewing surcharge; value: 0.25; display: $0.25 per record; kind: total; label: Ordinary courthouse copy; value: 1.0; display: Usually $1.00 per page; kind: total; label: Preliminary title search lower quote; value: 100; display: $100 lower endpoint; kind: total; label: Preliminary title search upper quote; value: 150; display: $150 upper endpoint; kind: total; label: Single probate lower quote; value: 4000; display: Approximately $4,000 lower endpoint; kind: total
